subject: VertexBank cost playback + pilot gating
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@vertexbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: VertexBank discovery — quick playback + next steps

Hi Tom — thanks again for taking time today. Quick playback from our end to make sure we captured priorities and to propose a narrow pilot scope so procurement/eng can evaluate cost and ops impact.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary pain: real-time fraud signal enrichment for loan approvals. Current pipeline is hitting token limits and inconsistent latency at peak hours.
- Business goal: bring model-powered approvals into production with <200ms median inference and predictable monthly spend.
- Success metrics: 95% approval latency <250ms, cost per approval < $0.12 (target), and a 2–3% lift in auto-approve rate within the first 3 months.

Workload profile you shared
- Monthly inference traffic: ~2M approvals (peaks to 12 qps for short bursts)
- Average prompt length: 250–450 tokens; expected average response 120 tokens
- Sensitive data: token-level PII; customer requires SOC2 + encrypted-at-rest keys

Cost/TCO anchors we discussed (rough order of magnitude)
- Baseline hosted inference estimate (no batching/cache): ~$6,800/mo for sustained 2M requests (per our quick model)
- With conservative batching + prefix caching (what we recommend for your workload): ~$2,200–3,100/mo (depends on hit rate and tolerated SLOs)
- Key levers: batch window (25–75ms), KV prefix cache (expected 20–35% hit rate), quantized model variant for less-costly throughput.

Risks / procurement constraints you flagged
- Monthly cap: procurement wants a firm monthly spend cap before committing to pilot.
- SLA: 99th percentile latency requirements will be evaluated; need to confirm whether 99th <400ms is an acceptable boundary for the pilot.

Proposed pilot (2–4 weeks)
- Narrow scope: inference for loan pre-approval flow only (no downstream scoring).
- Objectives: validate latency SLO, measure real caching hit rate in production traffic, and demonstrate cost per approval with Redwood Optimize suggestions.
- Deliverables: TCO workbook, per-route latency/cost dashboard access, and an operations checklist for rollout.
- Owners & timing: Soojin (RM) — design pilot plan by 6/18; Marissa (solutions eng) — pilot deployment and telemetry; VertexBank eng — provide sample traffic and acceptance criteria.

Attachments: I attached a short TCO workbook and a 1-pager on batching/caching levers to make the tradeoffs concrete.

Next asks (can you confirm by EOD Wednesday?)
1) Procurement: a target monthly cap (ballpark is fine) we should model against for the TCO workbook.
2) Eng: acceptance criteria for latency (median, p50/p95/p99) + who will run the first smoke tests.
3) Compliance: list of SOC2 / KMS requirements we need to verify before enabling private key integrations.

If that lines up, I’ll send a short one-page pilot SOW and a DocuSign link for the pilot terms so procurement can fast-track.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@vertexbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@vertexbank.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@vertexbank.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VertexBank discovery — quick playback + next steps

Soojin — thanks for the thorough write-up. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly cap: procurement prefers pilots under $5k/mo for authorization — if your TCO shows sub-$5k with caching, that would make getting signoff much faster.
- Latency SLO: engineering will be comfortable with p50 < 200ms and p95 < 320ms for the pilot; p99 target is negotiable but we need instrumentation to understand tail behavior.
- Data residency: we need confirmation that logs with PII are not retained in plaintext and that we can scope audit logs retention to 90 days.

Can you model a conservative scenario (20% cache hit, 30ms batching window) and an aggressive scenario (35% cache hit, 50ms batching with slightly higher median) and show cost per approval for both? If the conservative scenario is under $5k/mo we can fast-track.

Also looping in Sara (procurement) to coordinate DocuSign and a PO process.

Tom
VP, Product — VertexBank

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VertexBank discovery — quick playback + next steps (conservative + aggressive TCO)

Tom / Sara — per your ask, attached two quick scenarios in the TCO workbook. Here’s a high level summary so procurement/eng can act quickly.

Conservative scenario (what procurement asked us to model) - Cache hit: 20% - Batch window: 25–30ms (small batching to keep p95 low) - Expected monthly cost: ~$4,600/mo - Expected cost per approval: ~$0.092 - Latency estimate (based on our runtime perf): p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 310ms, p99 ~ 520ms (p99 may need model-variant or region fallback)

Aggressive scenario (higher batching & caching) - Cache hit: 35% - Batch window: 50ms (higher throughput) - Expected monthly cost: ~$2,850/mo - Expected cost per approval: ~$0.057 - Latency estimate: p50 ~ 160ms, p95 ~ 260ms, p99 ~ 420ms

Notes / tradeoffs
- The p99 numbers reflect tail amplification with variable prompt sizes; achieving p99 < 400ms requires either a smaller batch window or a quantized lower-latency model in the hot path. We can run a short micro-benchmark during the first 48–72hrs of pilot to decide which path.
- Cost includes Redwood hosted inference + 30% buffer for peak bursts; it assumes average prompt/response sizes you shared. If peak qps exceeds documented bursts we’ll need to enable reserved burst capacity (dedicated) which is an ops cost delta.
- Compliance: we can set log retention to 90 days and enable customer-managed KMS. We’ll send the SOC2 attestation and diagram this week.

Attachments: vertex_tco_estimate.xlsx (two scenarios) and redwood-batching-1pager.pdf (operational levers).

Next steps (I’ll take these on unless you delegate)
- 6/18: finalize pilot SOW and DocuSign link (Soojin)
- 6/19: procurement to confirm internal PO threshold (Sara)
- 6/22: tentative pilot kickoff if PO approved and test traffic available (Marissa + VertexBank eng)

If these numbers look right I’ll send a one-page SOW and DocuSign link today.

—
Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — the conservative scenario at ~$4.6k/mo looks like it will fit our pilot gating. A couple of procurement notes to speed things along:

- Please send the one-page SOW and the DocuSign link to procurement@vertexbank.com. We prefer a one-off pilot SOW under $10k with a month-to-month PO.
- For billing: we need to include a PO number on the invoice; I will confirm the PO range by Friday.
- For security: SOC2 attestation and KMS integration steps are required before pilot kickoff. Please send the SOC2 evidence and KMS checklist to security@vertexbank.com.

Assuming SOW is straightforward we can still aim for the 6/22 kickoff. Send DocuSign and I’ll circulate internally.

Sara Lin
Director, Procurement — VertexBank
